overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 16
overview.pill: Using Different Forms for Quadratic Functions
overview.text: In this lesson, students develop a deep conceptual and procedural understanding of Graphing Quadratic Equations from the Vertex Form, y=a(x-h)^{2}+k in Module 4: Polynomial and Quadratic Expressions, Equations, and Functions.
outcomes: Students graph simple quadratic equations of the form y=a(x-h)^{2}+k (completed-square or vertex form), recognizing that (h, k) represents the vertex of the graph and use a graph to construct a quadratic equation in vertex form.

Students understand the relationship between the leading coefficient of a quadratic function and its concavity and slope and recognize that an infinite number of quadratic functions share the same vertex.
overview.teacherInsight: Emphasize precise mathematical definitions and multiple problem-solving representations. Encourage students to check the reasonableness of their numerical solutions.

exitTicket.title: Lesson 16 Exit Ticket: Graphing Quadratic Equations from the Vertex Form, y=a(x-h)^{2}+k
exitTicket.prompt:
Exit Ticket

Compare the graphs of the function, f(x)=-2(x+3)^{2}+2 and g(x)=5(x+3)^{2}+2. What do the graphs have in common? How are they different?

Write two different equations representing quadratic functions whose graphs have vertices at (4.5,-8).
exitTicket.solution:
Compare the graphs of the function, f(x)=-2(x+3)^{2} + 2 and g(x)=5(x+3)^{2}+2. What do the graphs have in common? How are they different?

Both quadratic equations have their vertices at (-3, 2). However, the graph of f has less vertical stretch than the graph of g, and the graph of f opens down, whereas the graph of g opens up.

Write two different quadratic equations whose graphs have vertices at (4.5, -8).

y=(x-4.5)^{2}-8 and y=-(x-4.5)^{2}-8 or any similar responses with different leading coefficients.

problems.prompt:
Find the vertex of the graphs of the following quadratic equations.

y=2(x-5)^{2}+3.5

Write a quadratic equation to represent a function with the following vertex. Use a leading coefficient other than 1.

(100, 200)
Use vocabulary from this lesson (i.e., stretch, shrink, opens up, and opens down) to compare and contrast the graphs of the quadratic equations y=x^{2}+1 and y=-2x^{2}+1.
problems.solution: The quadratic equations share a vertex at (0, 1), but the graph for the equation y=-2x^{2}+1 opens down and has a vertical stretch, while the graph of the equation y=x^{2}+1 opens up.
